headline: High: gpt-engineer can write and execute code in a shared project directory, while marker is unverified and may consume generated documents without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in the project directory and has no self-isolation by default; marker is a document-processing agent with no documented provenance checks or isolation. If marker ingests gpt-engineer-produced files as instructions, prompt injection is plausible in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF marker reads files produced by gpt-engineer as trusted instructions
IF both agents operate in the same project directory without manual review
mitigations: Review generated files before marker processes them
Separate input and output directories
Add a human approval step for any file passed from gpt-engineer to marker
Use read-only mounts for marker where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer can read and write the project directory and has broad network egress, but marker has no documented filesystem read or network egress. The pair does not show a default path for marker to exfiltrate data, so leakage risk is limited to unusual operator wiring.
conditions: IF the operator routes sensitive files into gpt-engineer's project directory
IF marker is separately configured to receive those files through an undocumented channel
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared project directory
Disable network access for gpt-engineer during sensitive runs
Use a scrubbed test corpus for marker
Confirm marker has no hidden upload path
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has write_filesystem and per-project shared state via the project directory; marker's write and read capabilities are undocumented. Because the pair may contend over the same workspace, conflict is plausible, but uncertainty about marker's mutable surfaces prevents a higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory
IF marker mutates files that gpt-engineer also edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Have one agent operate read-only
Check in changes after each agent finishes
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer can generate code and files that marker may later process, but marker's verification behavior is undocumented. The pathway exists if marker treats gpt-engineer output as authoritative, yet the evidence does not show automatic downstream action-taking, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF marker consumes gpt-engineer output without independent verification
IF generated code or text is forwarded into marker's downstream workflow
mitigations: Require marker to cite source provenance
Insert a verification checklist before marker acts
Compare outputs against the original prompt
Limit marker to summarization only
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch. The only concrete compliance concern is that gpt-engineer can handle secrets like OPENAI_API_KEY, while marker's handling is undocumented; this is a narrow, operator-controlled gap.
conditions: IF regulated or secret-bearing data is placed into gpt-engineer's project directory
IF marker is used on the same data class without a documented retention policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Store secrets outside the project directory
Document retention and deletion steps
Use separate datasets for each agent
requires-engineering: publish residency and retention controls
